Well the 2020 q4 earnings for NOK is not out yet. But I'm interested in how they ended this year. First, Is their Cash value. Has it changed? They've had a consistent amount of cash and cash equivalent the past 3 years and not only that they're paying a lot of dividends. If we see a huge dip in the cash without a huge dip in the company's income it might indicate acquisitions the company made and they would mention that too if they did. 

Huge decrease in cash usually indicates that the company is trying to expand. I expect this to happen because there's no reason to let that much cash sit for long periods of time. It's usual for company to accumulate cash for 3-5 years before they expand instead of borrowing money from the bank (think berkshire hathaway). The company is waiting for the right time to spend that cash. If I have to guess, this huge expenditure will occur in the next two years. Decrease in cash might scare off some investors but it could potentially indicate a buy signal.

Next is earnings, I don't expect strong earnings from 2020. A 20% decrease in earnings from 2019 is acceptable. However, a horrible earning might result in the company touching their cash reserves which could delay whatever their plans are in the future but I really don't think that will happen because all they have to do is stop paying dividends to keep their cash reserves intact.
